outcome: Acute and severe morbidity (intensive care unit admission, blood transfusion)
Time to resumption of family activities
finding: Cesarean-delivered women had a higher risk of various postpartum morbidities, including surgical site pain and infection, lower abdominal pain, breast engorgement/mastitis, urinary incontinence, and weakness, compared to vaginally delivered women.
mod_finding: Cesarean-delivered women had a higher risk of acute and severe morbidity, surgical site pain and infection, lower abdominal pain, breast engorgement/mastitis, urinary incontinence, and weakness, and took longer to resume family activities compared to vaginally delivered women.
